title: Chapter 5. DOROTHY PICKS THE PRINCESS
chineseTitle: 第5章 琥宝石公主的选择

paragraphs.en: The children felt dejected after hearing the cold words of the vegetable prince. Just as they were about to follow him out, the Wizard gently touched Dorothy's shoulder.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子们听了蔬菜王子冷冰冰的话后感到沮丧。就在他们准备跟着他出去的时候，巫师轻轻碰了碰多萝西的肩膀。

paragraphs.en: "Wait!" he whispered.
paragraphs.zh: “等等！”他低声说道。

paragraphs.en: "Why?" she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: "Let’s pick the Royal Princess," suggested the Wizard. "She is surely ripe and will be our ruler once alive. She might treat us better than that heartless prince."
paragraphs.zh: “让我们选那位皇家公主吧，”巫师建议道，“她肯定已经成熟了，一旦复活，将成为我们的统治者。或许她对我们比那个冷酷的王子更好一些。”

paragraphs.en: Agreed, Dorothy said eagerly. They leaned over the bush and each grabbed one of the princess's hands.
paragraphs.zh: 同意了，多萝西兴奋地说。她们俯身向那丛灌木，各自抓起了公主的一只手。

paragraphs.en: "Pull!" shouted Dorothy. The stems broke, and they gently placed the princess on the ground.
paragraphs.zh: “拉！”多萝西喊道。茎秆断了，他们轻轻将公主放在地上。

paragraphs.en: The princess adjusted her hair and bowed gracefully. "Thank you," she said sweetly.
paragraphs.zh: 公主整理了一下头发，优雅地鞠了一躬。“谢谢。”她甜笑道。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard knelt and kissed her hand. Then, the prince’s voice was heard, urging them to hurry. He returned with his followers.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师跪下亲吻她的手。随后，王子的声音响起，催促他们快些。他带着随从回来了。

paragraphs.en: Seeing this, the princess faced him directly. The prince stopped and trembled when he realized she had been picked.
paragraphs.zh: 见此情景，公主直视着他。王子意识到自己被选中了，顿时停了下来，浑身微微颤抖。

paragraphs.en: "Sir," the princess declared, "you have wronged me greatly. These strangers saved me from your selfish rule."
paragraphs.zh: 公主说道：“阁下，您对我造成了极大的伤害。这些陌生人救我于您的自私统治之下。”

paragraphs.en: The prince admitted, "I did not know you were ripe." He then placed his star on her head, and everyone bowed to her. The prince left alone, his fate unknown to Dorothy and her friends.
paragraphs.zh: 王子承认道：“原来你已经成熟了。”说完，他将王冠戴在她的头上，众人纷纷向她行礼。王子独自离去，他的去向让多萝西和她的朋友们无从得知。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard walked through Mangaboo's vegetable gardens, bypassing bridges to cross streams by walking in mid-air. Dorothy wondered aloud why they could move so freely above ground. The Wizard suggested it might be due to their proximity to Earth’s center, where gravity is weaker.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西、泽布和巫师穿过芒加boo的蔬菜园，他们绕过桥梁，在半空中行走以跨越溪流。多萝西不禁问道，他们为何能在地面以上如此自由地移动。巫师猜测这可能是因为他们的位置接近地球中心，那里重力较弱。

paragraphs.en: "This must be a fairy country," Zeb mused, as Dorothy confirmed the presence of vegetable people and the ability for Eureka and Jim to converse normally.
paragraphs.zh: “这一定是个魔法王国，”赛布沉思道，当多萝西确认了植物人存在，并且欧瑞卡和吉姆能够正常对话时。

paragraphs.en: In the gardens, they feasted on strawberries, melons, and other unknown fruits. Meanwhile, the kitten constantly demanded milk or meat, calling the Wizard names because he couldn't provide it magically.
paragraphs.zh: 在花园里，他们尽情品尝着草莓、瓜果以及其他一些未知的水果。与此同时，那只小猫不停地索要牛奶或肉食，因为它无法从巫师那里得到魔法供给而叫他难听的名字。

paragraphs.en: Eureka accused the Wizard of not being a real wizard. He admitted, "I am only a humbug." Dorothy agreed that Oz's Wizard had always been a fraud, though she didn’t know how to explain his trick with the tiny piglets.
paragraphs.zh: 欧丽克指控巫师不是真正的巫师。巫师承认道：“我只是一个骗人的家伙。”多萝西同意奥兹的巫师一直是个骗子，不过她不明白他那头小猪仔变戏法的事到底是怎么回事。

paragraphs.en: Zeb and the kitten both claimed they had seen the pigs themselves, challenging the Wizard’s explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布和那只小猫都声称亲眼见过那些猪，对巫师的解释提出了质疑。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard confirmed, "You saw them because they were there. Now they're in my pocket." He produced the tiny piglets, setting them on the grass where they ran and nibbled.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师确认道：“你看见它们是因为它们就在那里。现在它们在我的口袋里。”他掏出那两只小猪崽，放在草地上，只见它们欢快地跑着、啃食着。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, what cunning things!" Dorothy exclaimed, petting one. A squeal from a piglet interrupted her: "Be careful!
paragraphs.zh: “哦，多聪明的小家伙！”多萝西一边抚摸着其中一只，一边脱口而出。这时，一声猪仔的尖叫声打断了她：“小心点！”

paragraphs.en: You're squeezing me!"
paragraphs.zh: 你可别再捏我了！

paragraphs.en: The Wizard was astonished. "They can talk too?" he murmured.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师惊讶不已：“他们还会说话？”他低声道。

paragraphs.en: Eureka asked, "May I eat one of them? I'm starving."
paragraphs.zh: 欧瑞卡问道：“我可以吃一个吗？我饿坏了。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy replied reproachfully, "What a cruel question! It would be dreadful to eat these dear little things."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西不满地回答：“多残忍的问题啊！吃掉这些可爱的小东西未免太可怕了。”

paragraphs.en: Another piglet grunted, "Cats are cruel things." The kitten yawned and said, "I'm not cruel. I just need to eat."
paragraphs.zh: 另一只小猪哼了一声：“猫真是残忍的东西。”小猫打着哈欠说：“我不是残忍，我只是需要吃饭罢了。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard sternly declared, "You cannot eat my piglets. They prove I am a wizard."
paragraphs.zh: 巫师严肃地宣布：“你不能吃我的小猪崽。它们证明我是一个巫师。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy asked, "Why so small? I've never seen such tiny pigs before."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问道：“怎么这么小？我可没见过这么迷你的小猪。”

paragraphs.en: "They're from the Island of Teenty-Weent," explained the Wizard, "where everything is small because it's a small island. A sailor brought them to Los Angeles and I traded nine circus tickets for them."
paragraphs.zh: “他们来自特尼特尼岛，”巫师解释说，“那里的东西都很小，因为那是一个小岛。一个水手把它们带到洛杉矶，我用九张 Circus 票换来了它们。”

paragraphs.en: The kitten wailed, sitting in front of Dorothy, "But what am I going to eat? There are no cows here for milk; or any mice, or even grasshoppers. If I can't eat the piglets, you may as well plant me and raise catsup."
paragraphs.zh: 小猫坐在多萝西面前哀鸣道：“可是我该怎么办呢？这里没有奶牛可以挤奶；也没有老鼠或蚱蜢。如果不能吃小猪崽，那你还不如把我种下去，收获番茄算了。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard suggested, "There might be fish in these brooks. Do you like fish?"
paragraphs.zh: 巫师建议说：“这些溪流里或许有鱼。你喜欢吃鱼吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Fish!" cried the kitten. "Do I like fish?
paragraphs.zh: “鱼！”小猫喊道，“我喜欢吃鱼吗？”

paragraphs.en: They're better than piglets—or even milk!"
paragraphs.zh: 他们比小猪崽还要可爱——甚至胜过乳猪！

paragraphs.en: "I'll try to catch some for you," said the Wizard.
paragraphs.zh: “我会试着给你捉一些来。”巫师说道。

paragraphs.en: "But won't they be vegetable-like, like everything else here?" asked the kitten.
paragraphs.zh: “可他们不会像其他一切事物一样变得植物般僵化吧？”小猫问道。

paragraphs.en: "I think not. Fish are not animals and as cold and moist as vegetables. There's no reason why they can't exist in this strange country."
paragraphs.zh: 我认为不可能。鱼不是哺乳动物，它们冰冷湿润，就像蔬菜一样。在这个奇异的国度里，它们完全可以存在。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard fashioned a hook with a pin and used a string from his pocket as a fishing line. He found a bright red blossom to use as bait, reasoning that fish are easily fooled by bright colors. After casting his line into a nearby brook, he soon felt a sharp tug indicating a bite.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师用一根针做了个钓钩，从口袋里掏出一段线当钓鱼线。他发现一朵鲜红的花朵，打算用它做诱饵，心想鱼儿容易被鲜艳的颜色骗到。于是，他将钓线投进了附近的一条小溪，很快便感到钓线上有明显的拉扯，表明已经有鱼上钩了。

paragraphs.en: Pulling in the string, he successfully landed a fat, round fish with glistening scales.
paragraphs.zh: 他用力一拉绳子，成功捕获了一条肥硕圆润、鳞片闪烁的鱼。

paragraphs.en: Eureka, the kitten, snatched the fish mid-air and swallowed it whole. "If it had any bones, I ate them," she said calmly as she cleaned her face. Dorothy noted Eureka's greediness but understood the kitten was hungry.
paragraphs.zh: 欧拉利卡，这只小猫，半空中抢过那条鱼并一口吞了下去。“要是鱼有骨头的话，我也一起吃掉了。”她冷静地说着，一边擦拭脸上的鱼汁。多萝西注意到欧拉利卡的贪吃，但理解小猫只是饿了而已。

paragraphs.en: The little pigs watched in fear as the scene unfolded. One remarked, "Cats are dreadful creatures!" Another added, "I'm glad we're not fishes!"
paragraphs.zh: 小猪们恐惧地注视着眼前的一幕。一只说道：“猫真是可怕的家伙！”另一只则接口道：“还好我们不是鱼呢！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy reassured them, "Don't worry; I won't let the kitten hurt you." She then remembered some leftover crackers from her train lunch and brought them to the buggy. Eureka sniffed at the food but the piglets eagerly ate it.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西安慰他们说：“别担心，我不会让小猫伤害你们的。”她想起自己火车午餐还剩下一些饼干，便拿给了马车上的小猪。欧丽卡闻了闻食物，但小猪们却迫不及待地吃了起来。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard suggested they return to the city. The cab-horse, who had been grazing nearby, agreed he was ready to go whenever Dorothy wished. After putting the pigs back in his pocket where they fell asleep, the group climbed into the buggy and Jim started back towards town.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师建议他们返回城市。那匹正在附近吃草的出租马同意随时准备出发，只要多萝西愿意。猪被放回口袋后很快就睡着了，大家爬上马车，吉姆便开车往镇上驶去。

paragraphs.en: "Where shall we stay?" Dorothy asked as they left.
paragraphs.zh: “我们去哪儿住呢？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard decided to take possession of the Sorcerer's House. "The Prince promised he would keep me until a new Sorcerer was chosen," said the Wizard. They agreed, and Jim drove them into the big door of the domed hall.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师决定接管术士的宅邸。“王子答应他会在我这里留到选出新的术士为止，”巫师说道。他们达成一致，吉姆驾车将他们送进了大厅那扇拱门的大门前。

paragraphs.en: "It doesn't feel very cozy," Dorothy observed, looking around at the bare room. "But it will do for now."
paragraphs.zh: “这里感觉不太温馨，”多萝西环顾着这间空荡荡的房间，说道，“但就暂时将就一下吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Look up there," Jim pointed to some openings near the top of the dome. "They seem like doorways, but no stairs lead to them."
paragraphs.zh: “看看那边，”吉姆指着穹顶顶部附近的一些开口说，“它们看起来像是门廊，但没有楼梯通向那里。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard suggested they walk in mid-air towards these openings. They climbed until they reached several doorways leading into upper halls. Inside, they found many small rooms with glass benches and tables, but no beds.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师建议他们悬在空中步行，朝着那些开口走去。他们越走越高，最终到达了几扇通向顶层大厅的门廊。里面有许多装有玻璃长凳和桌子的小房间，却没有床铺。

paragraphs.en: "Perhaps these people never sleep," Dorothy wondered aloud.
paragraphs.zh: 或许这些人从不睡觉，多萝西不禁出声猜测。

paragraphs.en: Zeb explained that the suns were always in the same position, so there was no night. "That makes sense," agreed the Wizard. He decided to rest on one of the hard glass benches.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布解释说，太阳始终处于同一位置，因此没有夜晚。“这倒是合情合理。”巫师点了点头，决定在其中一个坚硬的玻璃长椅上休息。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy chose a small room at the end of the hall and lay down. Zeb went back outside to unharness Jim, who promptly fell asleep with Eureka by his side. Then he returned to an upper room and soon joined Jim in slumber.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西选了一间位于走廊尽头的小房间躺了下来。泽布回去解开了吉姆的缰绳，只见吉姆立刻在尤里卡的陪伴下睡着了。随后，泽布回到楼上的一间房内，不一会儿也加入了沉睡之中。
